Description:
The Nauru Sustainable Urban Development Project (NSUDP) is designed to improve Nauru's water 
supply, sanitation, and solid waste management systems. Approved in November 2024, the initiative 
carries a total funding of USD 37.5 m and is supported by the Project Readiness Financing (PRF) fund of 
USD 5 m, initiated in August 2021 during the project's design phase.
In FY 2025-26, the project will transition into the next phase, which includes hiring a Contract 
Supervising Consultant (CSC) and initiating a tender process to select a contractor for civil construction 
works under the USD 37.5 m urban development initiative. For this fiscal year, ADB anticipates 
disbursing USD 1.2 m in in-kind assistance through the PRF to support the existing project management 
team overseeing the design phase. Additionally, approximately USD 370,000 will be disbursed for initial 
implementation activities. Once contracts are finalized for the CSC and civil works contractor, 
disbursement levels for the NSUDP are projected to increase significantly.

Description: Additionally, ADB will allocate an estimated USD 1 m (AUD 1.6 m) for technical assistance aimed at supporting the Improving Fiscal Sustainability Program. This initiative focuses on strengthening state_x0002_owned enterprises (SOEs), enhancing social protection frameworks, promoting gender equality, and advancing efforts within the climate change sector

Project Name: Sustainable and Climate Resilient Connectivity Project
Description:
The Sustainable and Climate Resilient Connectivity Project, also known as the Port Project, was 
approved by ADB in August 2018 with a budget of USD 62.28 m (AUD 91.56 m), including co-financing 
from the Australian Government and the Green Climate Fund. In 2022, ADB provided additional funding 
of USD 15 m (AUD 23 m) to cover the temporary accommodation expenses associated with the
relocation program for the Port Project.
For the fiscal year 2025-26, the remaining major works for this project include the installation of 
permanent protective measures for the Northern Container Yard revetment using specially designed 
rock bags, as well as achieving the target depth of the wharf basin. An estimated USD 8.4 m (AUD $13.5 
m) will be disbursed to cover construction costs and supervision fees for the project.

The Solar Power Development Project encompasses the installation of a 6MW solar energy farm, 
alongside institutional capacity development initiatives to support sustainable operations. This project, 
approved in September 2019, has a total budget of USD 22 m (AUD 32.34 m) and is intended to deliver 
positive impacts for Nauru households.
In the fiscal year 2025-26, following the commissioning of the solar grid into the Nauru Utility 
Corporation’s (NUC) national power system, an estimated USD 800,000 will be disbursed to the Joint 
Venture contractor and the Project Implementation Consultant for their services.

Under the Nauru-Australia Treaty (NAT) signed in December 2024, Australia will provide $100 million 
over five years in direct budget support to further strengthen Nauru’s economic security and resilience. 
This support will assist to give the Government of Nauru fiscal certainty to invest in Nauru’s future, 
including by making deeper and long-term investments in education, health and social services to 
enhance the well-being of the Nauruan people. 
Through the Treaty, Australia will ensure Nauru does not risk being de-banked again. The 
Commonwealth Bank of Australia commenced banking operations in Nauru in August 2025. 
Australia and Nauru will expand and deepen our security cooperation, committing to consult on 
developments that threaten our sovereignty, peace or stability. Australia commits to maintaining its 
standing as Nauru’s primary security partner through $40 million in new investments that will support 
Nauru’s policing and security needs. This includes Australian support for police and broader national 
22
security, capital infrastructure, training, equipment, recruitment and retention.

The $20m Nauru Education Program provides support to Nauru's education system and is aligned with Government of Nauru's policy frameworks and systems. The program funds advisers and education activities, as well as administration of the Australia Awards scholarships in Nauru. The program is continuing to 2027 under a managing contractor (TetraTech), with plans for a limited tender approach for the next phase from 2027. Nauru usually receives 10-20 places across the Australia Awards and Australia Awards Pacific annually depending on funding and applicants. Australia also supports direct-funding agreements (DFAs) to the Government of Nauru to fund education activities in Nauru including scholarships for Nauruans to study in Brisbane high schools, teacher salaries, licensing fees enabling Nauruan schools to offer the Queensland Certificate of Education, and partnership between the Nauru Department of Education and Queensland TAFE to deliver vocational education.

Australia has partnered with Nauru to support health outcomes for over 25 years. Post are streamlining multiple health work streams and advisers into one consolidated program. The new Rana Tsimorum (2025-2035) investment is a whole-of-health program that works with the Government of Nauru to ensure that Nauru’s health system is better able to respond to health threats and effectively deliver inclusive quality health services and population-level interventions for the people of Nauru. This program is made up of three components: health system strengthening, health service delivery, and inclusive health. It will continue existing successful workstreams including visits by surgical teams and veterinarians, inline advisers and health information improvements; while also opening up new work streams in priority areas identified by Nauru1.
Lead Organisation: Ministry of Health and Medical Services, Department of Public Health

Description:
Halting and reversing land degradation, as well as conserving remnant biodiversity in Small Island Developing States (SIDS), is a critical global priority. Nauru is among the most severely affected, with decades of unsustainable surface phosphate mining leaving much of the island’s landscape degraded and creating deep economic and social reliance on mining revenue. This legacy has hindered efforts to adopt Sustainable Land Management (SLM) and biodiversity conservation through an integrated landscape approach.

External support is essential to achieve systemic change—placing Nauru on a sustainable land-use pathway by mainstreaming Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) and restoring ecosystem services through the conservation and enhancement of the island’s limited biodiversity assets.

The proposed Project provides this transformational shift. It will establish enabling policy and regulatory frameworks for SLM and biodiversity conservation, integrate LDN targets into national development planning, and pilot restoration initiatives on severely degraded post-mining lands. Concurrently, it will safeguard and restore Nauru’s remaining forests and raise awareness and capacity at national and community levels to ensure long-term stewardship of rehabilitated landscapes.

The Pacific Community (SPC) will support implementation of the agreed activities under four key components of the Nauru Restoration Generation Project:

Component 1: Strengthening policy and institutional capacity for sustainable land management and biodiversity conservation.

Component 2: Rehabilitation and restoration of degraded land to protect and reinstate ecosystem services in Nauru.

Component 3: Conservation and sustainable use of Nauru’s forests.

Component 4: Scaling up efforts towards land degradation neutrality and biodiversity conservation.

This comprehensive approach directly addresses four critical barriers—policy gaps, technical and financial capacity constraints, degraded landscapes, and limited public awareness—through four interlinked outcomes. Together, these interventions will position Nauru on a sustainable trajectory, aligning with global LDN targets and the Sustainable Development Goals while contributing to regional SIDS priorities.
